title: Phase 4: policy, executor, intervention tiers, safety surface
description:
Phase 4 implementation epic.

BACKGROUND: policy + executor + the ADR-013/ADR-014 tier system. The only epic that can touch the system; every task is gated by SI-1..SI-8 and the ST suite. T3 act stays design-only.

MODE LADDER (read carefully; this wording was corrected on 2026-10-24 because the earlier note read as a loop):
1. OBSERVE - plans only, executes nothing. This is the default and the state after any fault.
2. CANARY entry condition: the path is implemented and its pre-canary evidence exists - for T4, an adapter with a cited EffectRange source and a passing ST-23 harness; for L2, a passing ST-24 harness. This is evidence that the mechanism works in a test fixture. It is NOT production evidence.
3. CANARY - executes within a strict budget while collecting production evidence: every invocation is compared against what observe would have done.
4. ENFORCE promotion condition: >= 20 canary invocations for that class, verified effect, no adverse events (constants.md). Promotion is manual, per class, and recorded.

So: pre-canary evidence answers 'does it work at all'; canary evidence answers 'does it work here'. They are different artifacts and neither substitutes for the other.

EXIT GATE: bead G-P4 (memory_pilot-532.1), not the epic itself.

ORDERING TRAP: do not build T4/L2 before P4EXEC's intent durability and per-class breakers exist.

REFERENCE: docs/00-product/roadmap.md Phase 4; docs/04-safety/action-authorization.md section 5.
notes:
[2026-10-23 10:35:52 UTC] EXECUTION ORDER: P4POLICY -> P4PLANNER -> P4EXEC -> (P4T1, P4T2 in parallel, then P4T4, P4L2, P4T5) -> P4LADDER.

THE V1 FENCE (read v1-scope-contract.md section 2 before writing any code): T1/T2/T4-framework/L2-managed/T5 are in. T3 act, L3 allowlist-terminate, L4 auto-intervention, and suspend-as-relief are OUT and have no executor code path. The single legal signal call site is stopOwnedChild(OwnedPid) per ADR-014 section 2. Adding any other signal path is not a code review decision; it is an ADR.

ORDERING TRAP: do not build T4/L2 before P4EXEC's intent-durability and breaker machinery exists. Both paths are externally effective; without intent records a crash makes them un-auditable, and without separate breaker classes a flaky adapter silently disables admission control.
